name: Thyroid/hypothyroid evaluation

lead: Thyroid evaluation is a blood-test workup for hypothyroidism, which can include facial puffiness among its signs.
Many cases have few symptoms, and facial puffiness has other causes too.

paras: Low thyroid hormone can cause fluid-like buildup in the skin (myxedema) and other changes; TSH is the first screening test [1].
Treatment is with prescribed levothyroxine, with dose monitored by TSH [1].

lead: Thyroid evaluation means testing for hypothyroidism, a condition in which the thyroid does not make enough hormone. In appearance discussions it is raised as a possible medical cause of a persistently puffy face [1].

Wikipedia lists a puffy face, particularly around the eyes, dry coarse skin, hair loss and loss of the outer eyebrows among signs of the condition, and describes a TSH blood test as the usual first step, with levothyroxine as standard treatment [1]. Evaluation is a clinical matter, and the wiki documents what clinical sources report.

paras: Reported features include facial puffiness around the eyes, pale expressionless look, dry skin, myxedema, hair thinning and loss of the outer eyebrows. Many people have mild or no symptoms [1].

A TSH test is the best first test, usually repeated several weeks later, with free T4 measured if TSH is high. Iodine deficiency is the most common cause worldwide, and Hashimoto thyroiditis is the most common cause where iodine is sufficient [1].

Clinical guidelines from bodies such as NICE and AACE/ATA address diagnosis and treatment of hypothyroidism [1]. No studies found specifically on thyroid testing as a looksmaxxing or de-puffing strategy.
